# sinter

> sinter binds JSON APIs to plain HTML: keyed resources cached from the server, kept current from server events, rendered through <template> bindings, with optimistic mutations. A build step compiles annotated HTML into a page module; the browser runs no parser and no eval.

Package: @tiaforge-ui/sinter. Every directive is a `data-sn-*` attribute or an `<sn-*>` element. Anything else is a build error with a suggestion.

Work in strict mode, so warnings fail like errors instead of scrolling past: `sinter({ strict: true })` in the Vite config (or `SINTER_STRICT=1`; the build type-checks when the project has TypeScript), `npx sinter check --strict` after every change, `render(html, { strict: true })` in tests (`render()` reads `SINTER_STRICT` too), and read the dev server's terminal, where strict mode prints the browser's runtime warnings. A clean exit means no warnings, not only no errors. Fix what a warning reports; do not turn strict mode off. Keep a code a warning only when the user agrees, in `strict: { allow: { SN504: 'reason' } }`. Details: docs/strict.md and "Type checking" below.

Read this once, and not again: to look something up later, run `npx sinter docs <topic>`, which prints one section (`layouts`), an attribute or element (`data-sn-for`, `sn-event`), a diagnostic (`SN318`) or the lines that have all of some words; `npx sinter docs` lists the topics. It prints this version's docs; sinter's docs on the web describe another version. To try a page and test what it does (each request with its headers, each resource's state, history, what a click changed), run `npx sinter render page.html --api http://localhost:<port> --click '<selector>'` against your running API, or with `--api mocks.json`, before writing browser or curl scripts (`--help` for the steps: input, select, back, …); a browser is only needed for layout and browser-specific behaviour. Paths under `docs/` name the longer guides, for people, in the repository (https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/tree/main/docs); `docs/diagnostics.md` ships in this package and `sinter docs SN…` prints from it.

This is the full reference, `llms-full.txt`. `llms.txt` beside it is the short version: the core reference and an index of these sections.

## Attributes

- `data-sn-state` (object literal): declares local reactive state for the element and its subtree
- `data-sn-let` (object literal {name: expression}): derived names for the element and its subtree, computed where they are read (a helper call included: keep an expensive one's results with `memo()`, configuration.md); later names may use earlier ones
- `data-sn-text` (value expression): sets textContent (null and undefined: empty, no `?? ''` needed); never HTML. On a <template>: a text node with no element (a run of text beside elements); no other attribute on that template
- `data-sn-attr` (object literal {href: …}): literal keys; null/false removes, true sets empty; URL values are checked; checked, selected, indeterminate and value also set the live property
- `data-sn-href` (URL template): on <a>, <area>: the link; may also start with ? or #
- `data-sn-class` (object literal {unread: …}): toggles each class
- `data-sn-style` (object literal {'--color': …}): sets each property with style.setProperty
- `data-sn-show` (value expression): toggles the hidden attribute
- `data-sn-prefetch` (off): on <html>: no other page prefetches this one's data or the page itself (Speculation Rules), and none prerenders it; for pages that do something when they load
- `data-sn-permanent` (name): with sinter({ swap }): kept as is (playing, scrolled) across a link to a page with the name; its bindings go on
- `data-sn-swap` (off): on <html>: links here load it; on a link: it loads its page
- `data-sn-transition` (value expression (a name)): the same thing on two pages: following a link from the element (or its row) to a page with an element of the same name morphs one into the other (view transitions; back too)
- `data-sn-with` (object literal): sets JS properties; custom elements only (also one defined later). On a component's tag: its props, live and read-only. On a <slot> declared Slot<T>: the values its fill reads as $slot; on a named <slot> its component does not declare, a tree placement, filled by the nearest enclosing component declaring the name
- `data-sn-props` (props type): the props a component or a layout takes, a TypeScript type literal, { article: Article; compact?: boolean }. On the <template> of a component file (src/components/<name>.html, or a component library's components/): a member cell: Slot<{ row: Row }> is a slot that passes data to its fill; its root renders at most one element (one element, a data-sn-if/data-sn-else chain of them, a component, <sn-component use> or a <slot>), or, a head component, any number of head elements (<title>, <meta>, <link>, …), inlined at its use in a head. On the <html> of a layout file (src/layouts/<name>.html): a page that is only the layout's tag fills its slots, in the head and the body. Either leaves it out when it takes no props
- `data-sn-early` (off): on a component's tag (a use): this use is left out of the early script and renders when the page module runs (build-time constants stay in the HTML); keeps the early script small
- `data-sn-import` (lazy packages, comma-separated): loads packages of sinter({ lazy }) when the element is rendered (at takeover outside templates, when its branch or row first renders inside one), instead of on first call
- `data-sn-wait` (off): on a box whose width follows its content (a flex item without a basis or width, a float) around a list over late data: what follows the box stays invisible while the list's first rows load (at most 3 s), so nothing shown moves when they widen it (builds, at the widths where it is so); off shows it, and SN529 says it moves
- `data-sn-preload` (lazy packages, comma-separated): the build preloads packages of sinter({ lazy }) with the page (<link rel="modulepreload">): fetched with the page bundle, run on first call or by data-sn-import
- `data-sn-ref` (name): in a component's markup: the element its script reads as this.refs.<name>, typed by its tag
- `data-sn-emits` (events type): on the <template data-sn-props>: the events emit() sends and their detail types, e.g. { select: Article }
- `data-sn-model` (state path | $url.<param>): two-way binding for form controls; on $url, the URL follows (a history entry; typing at each pause), and a <select multiple> or a checkbox with a value makes the parameter a list
- `data-sn-model-debounce` (duration): delays the model's write until typing pauses (no second pause after it); Enter writes at once
- `data-sn-for` (item in list | (item, i) in list): repeats a <template> per item. On <html>: the page once per entry of a `file:` list, at `data-sn-path` filled from it
- `data-sn-key` (value expression): row identity; inferred: resource key, object identity or value
- `data-sn-if` (value expression): renders a <template> while truthy. Same id, same control: when the branch with focus is swapped, the element with its id in the new one takes focus (a toggle's two buttons: <button id="follow" data-sn-delete=…> and <button id="follow" data-sn-post=…>)
- `data-sn-else`: on a <template> directly after an if template; with data-sn-if beside it, an else-if (<template data-sn-else data-sn-if="q">). Lists, branches and chosen components render between two comments (`<ul><!--sn 4--><li>a</li><!--/sn--></ul>`): CSS sees plain children. Comments that are exactly `<!--sn-->`, `<!--sn 4-->`, `<!--/sn-->` or `<!---->` are reserved (SN105); `$el` in an if, for or use is SN213; keep HTML comments
- `data-sn-options` (id of the list, or empty): arrows mark a [role=option|menuitem] of the list (empty: inside the element, else the nearest listbox or menu), Enter clicks it, Escape fires `sn-dismiss`; focus stays on the element. Text field: a combobox
- `data-sn-persist` (storage key): persists the model or state in localStorage under sn:
- `data-sn-post` (URL template): POST action
- `data-sn-put` (URL template): PUT action
- `data-sn-patch` (URL template): PATCH action
- `data-sn-delete` (URL template): DELETE action
- `data-sn-call` (action call): local action: a function of the actions module, e.g. pgp.decrypt(msg); a handler starts it with run('id'). The function gets a trailing context; its `ctx.request(url, { method, body })` encodes `body` as JSON: pass the object, not `JSON.stringify(…)` (a string)
- `data-sn-body` (value expression): JSON request body; overrides form serialization
- `data-sn-trigger` (DOM event name): overrides the default trigger
- `data-sn-debounce` (duration): delays the action's trigger, resets on each event
- `data-sn-concurrency` (block | queue | latest): what a trigger does while the action runs; default block for forms, queue otherwise
- `data-sn-optimistic` (handler expression): merge/upsert/remove calls applied before the request, kept on success, rolled back on failure
- `data-sn-then` (handler expression): runs after a 2xx response; $result = parsed body
- `data-sn-catch` (handler expression): runs after an error; $error = {status, body, message, detail}. A form without it shows a 4xx `{errors: {name: message}}` on its fields (aria-invalid and the message); its markup reads the failure as `$error`
- `data-sn-confirm` (value expression): asks this question before the action runs (configure({ confirm }), window.confirm by default); no question when falsy
- `data-sn-encoding` (form): the body (data-sn-body, arrays as repeated keys, or the form) goes as application/x-www-form-urlencoded
- `data-sn-retry` (retry policy name): sends the request again (with data-sn-call: each request ctx.request sends) as that policy of configure({ retry }) says (after a network error, a 5xx, a 429), with an Idempotency-Key; without it a write is sent once
- `data-sn-write-through` (off): turns write-through off for this mutation: its response is not applied to the resources it is about
- `data-sn-path` (URL patterns /a/:b …): on <html>: the path shapes this page is served for; `:name` segments appear read-only in $url
- `data-sn-resource` (resource name): on <script type="application/json"> in <head>: initial data for a resource
- `data-sn-on-<event>` (handler expression): plain event handler, no request; e.g. data-sn-on-click
- `data-sn-on-keydown-<key>` (handler expression): runs only for that key (also on-keyup-<key>): modifiers first, the key last, e.g. data-sn-on-keydown-j, -shift-n (N), -mod-enter (Ctrl, Cmd on Apple), -escape, -question (?); matches KeyboardEvent.key; other Ctrl/Alt/Meta held do not match; an ancestor's filter skips keys typed into fields; a match calls preventDefault()
- `data-sn-debounce-<event>` (duration): delays only that event's data-sn-on-<event> handler (it runs with the last event); e.g. data-sn-debounce-input

Key filters (`data-sn-on-keydown-<modifiers->key`, `data-sn-on-keyup-…`): modifiers `ctrl`, `alt`, `shift`, `meta`, `mod`, then one key: `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `escape`, `enter`, `tab`, `space`, `backspace`, `delete`, `insert`, `home`, `end`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, `arrowup`, `arrowdown`, `arrowleft`, `arrowright`, `contextmenu`, `f1`–`f12`, and characters by name: `slash` (`/`), `backslash` (`\`), `question` (`?`), `period` (`.`), `comma` (`,`), `semicolon` (`;`), `colon` (`:`), `quote` (`'`), `backquote` (``` ` ```), `minus` (`-`), `plus` (`+`), `equal` (`=`), `asterisk` (`*`), `bracketleft` (`[`), `bracketright` (`]`). Names are lowercase (N is `shift-n`). Filters on an ancestor skip keys typed into fields and Enter/Space on buttons and links; a match calls `preventDefault()`. The nearest element that handles an event wins; a key a plain handler does not `preventDefault()` goes on to its ancestors, so page-wide shortcuts go on `<body>`. Bubbling custom events (`emit()`, custom elements' events, `sn-error`, `sn-dismiss`) run every handler from the target up until one calls `$event.preventDefault()`; `stopPropagation()` does not end the walk.

## Elements

- `<sn-resource>` `name`, `src`, `method`, `body`, `call`, `for`, `key`, `items`, `total`, `order`, `when`, `paginate`, `type`, `cache`, `refresh`, `then`, `early`, `drafts`, `fields`: a named, page-wide cache of server data; `cache` (or `cache="10m"`) shows the data from the last page load at once, then revalidates. `early="off"`: never preloaded or requested before the page module (for a resource a request middleware answers itself; one whose request a middleware changes, such as a token, needs nothing: the build and runtime handle it). With `sinter({ apis })`, `src` is a path relative to an API (`/articles`, `billing:/invoices`); `method="POST"` with `body` loads with a POST of that value. `src="file:./intro.txt"` (`file:/…` from the root) reads the project at build time (text, JSON, markdown's frontmatter and `body`; a glob: a list with `slug`, `dir`, `path`), a constant (`order`, `drafts`; `fields="slug,title"`: only those fields of each entry ship to the browser, which a `content:` collection that browser code reads needs). Loading needs no attributes: concurrent loads of one URL share a request, a `src` change aborts the running one (latest wins), a change typed into a text field waits 250 ms for the next keystroke, a resource only dialogs read is requested with low priority, and a bfcache restore or going back online reloads. `paginate="{ keyset: { before: $item.id }, size: 20 }"` loads a page at a time (`append`, `numbered: true`; `model: $url.page` keeps a numbered list's page in the URL; `jump`, `params`, `directions`, also per API)
- `<sn-sync>` `src`: one server event stream
- `<sn-component>` `use`, `data-sn-with`, `data-sn-early`: a component chosen by data at runtime; `use` names it: ``use="`${b.type}-block`"`` (convention), `use="{ hero: 'hero-block' }[b.type]"` (map) or `use="blockComponent(b)"` (helper); it must fit `ComponentName`, every candidate must exist, props are checked per candidate (narrowed for convention and map); a value outside the candidates renders nothing, or the `data-sn-else` template after it; `data-sn-early="off"` leaves it out of the early script
- `<sn-event>` `name`, `resource`, `op`, `value`, `when`, `then`, `type`: maps one server event to a change message; child of <sn-sync>. `then`: a handler run after the change

## Expressions and scope

- Attribute values are JavaScript expressions, checked at build time. Value expressions (text, attr, class, show, for, if, key, body, state, URL interpolations) cannot assign, use `++`, `delete`, `await` or `import()`.
- Handlers (`data-sn-on-*`, `then`, `catch`) are statements separated by `;`: assignments to state, `$url.<param>` and `$locale`, and calls. No declarations or loops.
- `$url` is bindable: `data-sn-model="$url.q"` (query parameters; path parameters are read-only), `paginate="{ numbered: true, size: 10, model: $url.page }"` on a numbered list (the URL is then the list's single source: `page()` writes it, a filter change starts at page 1). History works as in a single-page app: user events add an entry, typing commits at each pause, other writes replace. Values are written as a reload reads them (strings; `true` as `'1'`; `false`/`null`/`''`/`[]` delete the parameter): use `+$url.page` for arithmetic. A parameter bound to a `<select multiple>` or checkboxes with a `value` is a list (`[]` when absent; SN211). Guide: docs/navigation.md#the-url-and-the-history.
- A handler cannot call an action function (SN203). To start an action from a handler (a key filter, `data-sn-then`, `<sn-resource then>`), give the action element an `id` and call `run('id')`; the element's busy state, concurrency, optimistic layer and `then`/`catch` apply. A hidden carrier works: `<span hidden id="mark-read" data-sn-call="mail.markRead(open)"></span>`. See the recipe "Run an action from a handler".
- `then` on `<sn-event>` is a handler run after the event's change is applied: the payload is `$event` (`$event.id`), the state around the `<sn-sync>` is in scope and assignable, its `data-sn-let` names are read-only, store functions work (`closeDialog('id')` names its dialog: there is no element). With `then`, `resource` and `op` may be left out.
- `then` on `<sn-resource>` is a handler run after each successful load (first load, `refresh()`, refresh events, `src` changes, every `page()`; per source on a `for` resource), not for cached data shown at once, failed loads or optimistic/event changes. `$result` is what the load stored (what `items` selects; the page just loaded). The state around the resource is in scope and assignable; `closeDialog('id')` names its dialog. It runs on every reload, so a once-only handler guards itself, one step per guard: `then="draft = $result ?? draft; $result && openDialog('compose')"`.
- Server errors on a form: a mutation without `data-sn-catch` on a form, or on a button or control inside one, that fails with a 4xx and a JSON body `{errors: {<name>: message | message[]}}` marks each control with that `name`: `aria-invalid="true"` and the message in the element its `aria-errormessage` names, else in a `<small data-sn-error data-tone="danger">` inserted after it; the first such field gets focus; editing a field clears its error, sending again clears all. Inside the form, `$error` is its last failed send (`{status, body, message, detail}`, or `null`; null again when sent again): show the rest with bindings, e.g. `<template data-sn-if="$error"><p data-sn-text="$error.detail"></p></template>`. Shown (no `sn-error`, no `onError`) when every message marked a field or the form reads `$error`. `data-sn-catch` opts out. Another response format: `configure({ fieldErrors: (error, {url, method}) => ({ name: messages }) })` reading `error.body` (`null`: mark no field; `undefined`: the default reading); codes instead of text: map them to `m.key()` there.
- `refresh="30s"` on `<sn-resource>` reloads it in the background once its last load is that old (not while the tab is hidden or `when` is falsy; `$meta.loading` stays false). A reload with an unchanged `ETag` (else `Last-Modified`) is not re-rendered, `then` still runs; servers send `ETag` with `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
- `data-sn-optimistic` may only call `merge`, `upsert`, `remove`. The change shows at once, stays when the request succeeds (committed under what `then` writes) and is rolled back when it fails. With an inline edit, leave edit mode when the form is sent, not in `then` (which waits for the server): `<form data-sn-patch="/api/items/{i.id}" data-sn-optimistic="merge(i, { title })" data-sn-on-submit="editingId = null" data-sn-catch="…">`. The request, the rollback and `catch` still run after the form is gone.
- A name resolves innermost first: loop variables, then the nearest `data-sn-state`, then resources, then magic names, helpers and store functions, then JavaScript globals. Browser APIs (`window`, `document`, `fetch`, timers, …) are refused: use a component's script.
- Resources are read-only: copy an item with `structuredClone(c)` to edit it, write with `merge()`.
- Helpers are plain function calls, never pipes: `date()`, `relative()`, `number()`, `bytes()`. Helper namespaces: `m.inbox_title()`.
- URL templates (actions, `src`, `data-sn-href`): `/api/x?id={c.id}`; interpolations are URL-encoded; the template must start with a literal `/path` or `https://origin`. A whole query value that is `null`/`undefined` or an empty array leaves the parameter out; an array is a repeated key (`?cal={cals}` → `cal=a&cal=b`); an array in the path is refused. A link's may also start with `?` or `#` (`?tag={$url.tag}&page={n}`); `data-sn-attr` keeps an `href` that comes whole from data (`i.href`).
- Use `$now` instead of `Date.now()` so bindings update. `$now` and `$meta.<name>.loadedAt` are `Date`s: compare and add with numbers through `$now.getTime()` (`$now.getTime() - Date.parse(t.createdAt) < 60_000`), or in a helper.

## Components

- A component is a file `src/components/<name>.html` (the name has a `-`), used as `<name>` on any page. It holds one `<template data-sn-props="{ article: Article; compact?: boolean }">` and optionally a `<style>`. Its root renders at most one element: one element, a `data-sn-if`/`data-sn-else` chain of them (`<template data-sn-if="href"><a …></a></template><template data-sn-else><button …></button></template>`), another component's tag (a variant with no wrapper), `<sn-component use>` or a `<slot>`; more, or text, is SN312. The tag's attributes land on each branch, on the element a component tag renders, on a fill; a constant prop decides the chain at build time. A component with a script or root `data-sn-state` keeps one plain element. `id`, `data-sn-model`, an action or `data-sn-transition` on the tag of a component whose root may render nothing: SN334. `data-sn-emits="{ select: Article }"` on the template declares its events.
- Every use is expanded at build time: the root element replaces the tag, so the component renders in the first frame like page markup and needs no runtime. The caller's `class` is joined with the root's; other attributes, handlers (`data-sn-on-<event>`), actions, `data-sn-class`, `-attr`, `-href`, `-style`, `-show` move onto the root in the caller's scope.
- Props go in with `data-sn-with="{ article: a, compact: narrow }"`: each is the caller's expression, live and read-only. An optional prop not passed is `undefined`, or the root's `data-sn-state` field of the same name. The component sees only its props, its own state, resources, helpers and magic names; slot content (`<slot>`, `<slot name="meta">` with fallback content, filled by the caller's children and `slot="meta"`) sees the caller's scope.
- Events come out with `emit('select', article)` (names checked against `data-sn-emits`); the caller handles them with `data-sn-on-select`, `$event.detail` typed. `data-sn-model="draft.stars"` binds a component that declares a `value` prop and a `change` event.
- A component with a script: `src/components/<name>.ts` beside its HTML, `export class TaskRing extends TaskRingComponent` (imported from `./task-ring.html`, typed by the generated `src/sinter.components.d.ts`). sinter creates it per instance and calls `connected()` (markup rendered, refs set), `propsChanged()` and `disconnected()`; it reads `this.props`, writes `this.state` (renders), uses `this.refs.<name>` (`data-sn-ref` in its markup), `this.root` and `this.emit()`. It writes only state, never nodes sinter renders. Use it for browser work (canvas, libraries, timers) instead of a custom element.
- A component may use itself (a tree: comments and replies) when the inner use is inside a `data-sn-for` or `data-sn-if` template (else SN306): `<template data-sn-for="r in comment.replies" data-sn-key="r.id"><comment-thread data-sn-with="{ comment: r }"></comment-thread></template>`. `merge(r, …)` and `remove(r)` change a nested item along its path at any depth; `upsert(comment.replies, x)` adds to a nested list. Nested loops need `data-sn-key`.
- `<sn-component use="`${b.type}-block`" data-sn-with="{ block: b }">` picks a component per item: a template string, a map in the markup (`use="{ hero: 'hero-block' }[b.type]"`) or a helper; it must fit `ComponentName` (`b.type + '-block'` is a `string`: write the template string); a `data-sn-else` template after it renders for a value outside the candidates.
- `data-sn-early="off"` on a component's tag (`<tag-cloud data-sn-early="off">`) leaves that use out of the early script (smaller head script; it renders when the page module runs, so it may shift the layout then).
- `<template data-sn-text="p.text"></template>` renders a text node with no element (search highlighting, a list joined with commas, runs of text beside elements); no other attribute on that template (SN333; wrap it for `data-sn-if`/`data-sn-for`).
- Component libraries: `sinter({ libraries: ['@acme/ui'] })` names packages whose package.json has `"sinter": "./sinter"`, a folder with `components/` (public), `components/internal/` (the library's own), `sinter.helpers.ts` and `sinter.types.ts`. Their public components are tags like the app's; names share the library's prefix (`ui-`), which no app component may use (SN337); an internal or unknown one is SN339. Helpers: `export * as ui from '@acme/ui'` in `src/sinter.helpers.ts`, then `ui.initials(x)`. Library types: `export type { Item } from '@acme/ui'` in `src/sinter.types.ts`. Its scoped styles are in `@layer sinter-lib`, declared first, so the app's CSS wins. No shadowing: wrap a library component in one of your own. Tree slots stop at the package. A library's repository runs `sinter check` over its `fixtures/*.html`. SN337: not a library; SN537 (warning): sinter outside its `peerDependencies` range. Guide: docs/libraries.md.
- A head component is a file `src/components/<name>.html` whose `<template data-sn-props="{ title?: string }">` holds head elements only, any number of them (`<title>`, `<meta>`, `<link>`, `<script>`, `<style>`, `<noscript>`, `<base>`, `<template data-sn-if>`, slots, other head components), inlined at its use in a `<head>` with no wrapper. Its tag takes only `data-sn-with` and slot content. A head component in a body, a component in a head, a body element in a head component: SN320.
- In a head, `<title data-sn-text>` binds, and a `<meta>` with a literal `name`, `property` or `itemprop` binds its `content`: `<meta name="description" content="Fallback" data-sn-attr="{ content: post?.summary ?? 'Fallback' }">`. Nothing else in a head binds (SN207). Constants are written into the HTML at build time; values from data render when it arrives, so scrapers that run no script see the literal content. A second `<title>`, `<meta name="description">`, `og:title`… in one head is SN321.
- A slot that is slot content of a component's tag forwards what fills it: `<seo-tags><slot name="seo" slot="extra"></slot></seo-tags>` puts the caller's `slot="seo"` content into `seo-tags`'s `extra` slot, in the caller's scope.
- One plain `<slot>` of a name may be placed in each branch of one `data-sn-if`/`data-sn-else` chain (its content is copied into each); two that can render together: SN312.
- A slot that passes data is a member `cell: Slot<{ row: Row; column: keyof Row }>` of the props type literal (no `?`, not a prop: passing it in `data-sn-with` is SN313; not in a head component's or a layout's props; `Slot` is sinter's type). The placement passes values with `<slot name="cell" data-sn-with="{ row: r, column: c }"><span data-sn-text="r[c]"></span></slot>`; the fill, `<b slot="cell" data-sn-text="$slot.row[$slot.column]"></b>`, sees the caller's scope plus `$slot` (`merge($slot.row, …)` acts on the caller's resource; an inner fill's `$slot` hides the outer one). A `<template slot="cell" data-sn-if>` starts an if/else chain. The placement's default is one plain element (or an if/else chain of them); an unnamed `<slot>` in the fill places that element's children. A `<slot>` no component or fill encloses, and other slot mistakes: SN331. A literal `id` in a `data-sn-for` row or a fill placed twice: SN532 (warning). A named `<slot data-sn-with>` its component does not declare is a tree placement: the nearest enclosing component declaring the name fills it, through components used inside one another (a root in a fill starts again; one in its own markup passes the outer fill through; every declared slot is placed somewhere; no root: SN331; a name close to a declared one: SN535, warning).

## Layouts

- A layout is a whole document `src/layouts/<name>.html` (the name has a `-`) whose `<html>` declares its props: `<!doctype html><html lang="en" data-sn-props="{ title?: string; nav: string }"><head>…<slot name="head"></slot></head><body>…<slot></slot></body></html>`. It has any number of named slots in its head and body; the default slot is in the body (a default slot in the head: SN318). No script beside it, no `data-sn-emits`. A layout without props needs no `data-sn-props`.
- A page that uses it is only its tag: `<site-layout data-sn-path="/post/:slug" data-sn-state="{ tab: 'all' }" data-sn-with="{ nav: 'post', title: post?.title }">…</site-layout>` (anything else on the page, or the tag anywhere else: SN318). Children fill the slots; a head element goes to a head slot with `slot="head"` (a `<title>`/`<meta>`/`<link>` for a body slot: SN320). Plain attributes on the tag replace the layout's on `<html>` (`lang`, `dir`; `class` is joined); `data-sn-path` and `data-sn-prefetch` go onto `<html>`. Handlers on the tag are the page's `<body>` handlers (on the layout's `<body>`, ahead of its own): DOM events, `sn-error` and `sn-dismiss` only (SN315), e.g. `data-sn-on-sn-error` and `data-sn-on-keydown-shift-n`.
- `data-sn-state` on the tag is the page's state: the props and all slot content see it, the layout's markup does not. The layout's markup sees its props, its own state, the page's resources and the globals.
- The merge happens before anything reads the page: early scripts, preloads, embedded data, Google Fonts and Vite's bundling of the layout's `<script type="module">` and stylesheets work on the merged document. Relative URLs in the layout (`./site.css`) are relative to the layout file. Layouts are not pages: leave `src/layouts/` out of the build's inputs (SN318).

## What belongs in markup

- Markup holds filters, conditions, single assignments and short calls. Logic goes into a helper when it computes a value (pure: unit-test it without a page), or into an action when it has side effects (`data-sn-call`).
- Handlers apply a helper's result to state: `data-sn-on-click="sel = rowClick($event, sel, f.id, ids)"`, not branches on `$event.shiftKey` in the attribute. See the row selection recipe.
- One step per condition: `open && closeDialog('detail')` is fine; `a && (b = null, closeDialog())` is not: split it into statements, let the dialog's `data-sn-on-close` reset state, or compute the new state in a helper.
- Warning SN507 (`complex-expression`) flags expressions that outgrew markup and names the limit it passes: statements per handler (4), comma sequences (0), steps behind one `&&`/`||`/`?:` statement (1), `?:` nesting (2), operations in an arrow function (8), operations per expression (15). `complexity: { level: 'error' }` fails the build on it, `complexity: false` turns it off.

## Magic names

`$event`, `$el`, `$url`, `$now`, `$locale`, `$result`, `$error`, `$meta`. `$event` in handlers (TypeScript types `$event.target` as any `EventTarget`: on an input, select or textarea read `$el.value`, the element the handler is on, typed by its tag; on an ancestor such as a form or a list, `$el` is the ancestor, so put the handler on the element, use `data-sn-model`, or narrow it: `/** @type {HTMLInputElement} */ ($event.target).value`), `$result` in `then`, `$error` (`{status, body, message, detail}`; `detail`: the server's words or null) in `catch`; `$meta.<resource>` has `loading`, `error`, `loadedAt`, `total`, `live` (`'connecting'`, `'open'` or `'retrying'` for a resource a `<sn-sync>` event feeds, the worst of its streams; `null` otherwise), and with `paginate`: `page` (numbered), `pages`, `from`, `to`, `hasPrev`, `hasNext` (no `pending`: an element shows its own request with `aria-busy`; SN303). Only where they apply: `$item` in `paginate`'s cursor, the item at the page's edge (`keyset: { before: $item.id }`); `$slot` in a fill of a slot declared `Slot<T>`, the values its placement passes (`$slot.row`); `$site` and `$canonical` with `sinter({ site })`, the site's root URL and the page's absolute URL, anywhere on a page (without `site`: SN323).

## Store functions

`refresh()`, `upsert()`, `merge()`, `remove()`, `page()`, `openDialog()`, `closeDialog()`, `emit()`, `run()`, `navigate()`: `refresh(people)` (the resource itself, not its name; several: `refresh(a, b)`), `upsert(people, item)`, `merge(item, {…})`, `remove(item)` (no resource name: they act on the item in the resource it came from, found by key: a row of a `data-sn-for` over a resource, also through `filter`/`toSorted` or a helper given one resource; an element (`list[0]`, `.find(…)`); a single resource; a prop or emitted detail that is one; state assigned one, `sel = m` or `structuredClone(m)`; anything else is SN317), `page(messages, 'next' | 'prev' | 'first' | 'last' | n)` (a page number needs a numbered list or keyset with `jump: true`, else SN304; a computed direction such as `$event.shiftKey ? 'prev' : 'next'` works everywhere, typed by `sinter check`; `prev` does nothing while `hasPrev` is false and `next` while `hasNext` is false, in every mode, so paging needs no `$meta` guard; `first` and `last` always load), `openDialog('id')` opens a dialog by its literal id, `closeDialog()` the nearest dialog or `closeDialog('id')` that one, `emit('event', detail)` (a bubbling, cancelable `CustomEvent`), `navigate(url)` (to this page with only parameters it reads changed: in the page, as a same-page link; else the browser loads it; `{ replace: true }`: in the current history entry), `run('id')` starts the action of the element with that literal id (SN309), as its trigger would but with `$event` null; a form is submitted (`requestSubmit()`, validation runs); a disabled or inert element does nothing; it returns nothing, results go to the element's `then`/`catch`. `$meta[…]` takes the resource too; a quoted name is SN301 (`refresh('people')`). The resource may be chosen: `page(searching ? results : messages, 'next')`, `||`/`??` between resources, or a `data-sn-let` name whose value is one (`data-sn-let="{ shown: searching ? results : messages }"`, then `page(shown, 'next')`, `$meta[shown].hasNext`); each one it can take is checked; a state variable, a helper result or `a && b` is SN301 (make it a `?:` between resources).

## Write-through

A mutation's 2xx response is applied to the store by itself, before `then` runs (the `write-through` module, loaded when a page has something to apply). With an OpenAPI spec: an object of a named schema in the response (`{article: Article}`) patches the same-key item in every list of that schema and what the URL named (`{article.slug}` names the single `article`; `{article.author.username}` also names `article.author`, a Profile); a POST to exactly a list's current URL inserts the created item (the response's, else body + returned key, else a reload; a filtered or paginated list is never inserted into); a PUT/PATCH body patches the entity the URL named. Without a spec: a DELETE of a row's URL (the list's URL plus one segment, from `c.id` with `c in comments`) removes the row, and a PUT/PATCH body patches the row when its keys are fields of the row. Patches merge and skip unchanged fields; `then` writes land on top. So `data-sn-then="merge(a, $result.article)"`, `upsert(comments, $result.comment)` and `remove(c)` are not written (SN510 says so); `data-sn-optimistic` is still how a change shows before the answer. `data-sn-write-through="off"` turns it off for one element.

## Retries

Nothing is sent again unless a retry policy says so. Policies are named in the config module: `import { retry } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/retry'; configure({ sessionProbe: '/api/user', retry: retry({ policies: { drafts: { backoff: ['1s', '30s'] }, network: { backoff: ['1s', '10s'], retries: 3 } }, get: 'network' }) })` (fields: `backoff: [first, longest]`, `retries`, `maxAge`, `key`: the header, default `Idempotency-Key`, or `false`). A write opts in on its element: `data-sn-retry="drafts"` (mutations only; writes have no default). `get` is the policy of every GET except background refreshes. A network error waits, then the session probe decides (2xx: send again, 401: lost to the login redirect); a 5xx is a failed try; a 429 or 503 waits for `Retry-After` and fails at once when that is after the policy's last try; a retried DELETE that gets 404 succeeded; other 4xx fail at once. Each trigger sends one idempotency key on every try. A server that ignores the key may create a duplicate from a retried POST: create with a client id (`PUT /api/notes/{uuid}`). While a write waits, its element keeps `aria-busy` (show "not saved" with `body:has(form[aria-busy])`), its optimistic change stays, `latest` replaces it with a newer trigger (use it for drafts: `block` keeps a form disabled), and leaving the page asks first (not on iOS).

## Recipes

Each recipe has a test beside it (`docs/recipes/<name>.test.ts`).

### List with filter

```html
<sn-resource name="people" src="/api/people" items="people" key="id" order="name"></sn-resource>

<section data-sn-state="{ q: '' }">
  <input type="search" placeholder="Search" data-sn-model="q">
  <p data-sn-show="$meta.people.loading" aria-busy="true">Loading…</p>
  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="p in people.filter(p => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q.toLowerCase()))">
      <li data-sn-text="p.name"></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
</section>
```

### Form dialog with repeatable fields

```html
<sn-resource name="people" src="/api/people" key="id" order="name"></sn-resource>

<section data-sn-state="{ draft: null }">
  <button data-sn-on-click="draft = {name: '', emails: [{value: ''}]}" commandfor="edit" command="show-modal">New</button>
  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="p in people">
      <li>
        <span data-sn-text="p.name"></span>
        <button data-sn-on-click="draft = structuredClone(p)" commandfor="edit" command="show-modal">Edit</button>
      </li>
    </template>
  </ul>

  <dialog id="edit">
    <!-- `upsert` puts the saved person into the list: a page without an OpenAPI spec has no write-through
         for a POST. With one (`sinter({ apis })`), write-through inserts it by itself; leave `upsert` out (SN510).
         No data-sn-catch: a failed save keeps the dialog open, with the server's messages on the fields. -->
    <form data-sn-post="/api/people" data-sn-body="draft"
          data-sn-then="upsert(people, $result); draft = null; closeDialog()">
      <p data-tone="danger" data-sn-show="$error && !$error.body?.errors" data-sn-text="$error?.detail ?? $error?.message"></p>
      <input name="name" data-sn-model="draft.name" required>
      <template data-sn-for="(e, i) in draft.emails">
        <input type="email" data-sn-model="draft.emails[i].value">
      </template>
      <button type="button" data-sn-on-click="draft.emails.push({value: ''})">Add email</button>
      <button type="submit">Save</button>
    </form>
  </dialog>
</section>
```

### Server validation errors on the fields

```html
<!-- Server validation errors: no data-sn-catch, so a 4xx with {errors: {email: "…"}} marks the field
     aria-invalid and shows the message after it (temper styles aria-invalid); `aria-errormessage`
     puts a message where you want it. Inside the form, `$error` is its last failed send: here a
     line for a failure that is not about a field (a 5xx). -->
<form data-sn-post="/api/signup" data-sn-then="emit('signed-up', $result)">
  <p data-tone="danger" data-sn-show="$error && !$error.body?.errors" data-sn-text="$error?.detail ?? $error?.message"></p>
  <label>Email <input type="email" name="email" required></label>
  <label>Username <input name="username" required aria-errormessage="username-error"></label>
  <small id="username-error" hidden></small>
  <button>Sign up</button>
</form>
```

### SSE sync

```html
<sn-resource name="people" src="/api/people" key="id" order="name"></sn-resource>

<main data-sn-state="{ sel: null }">
  <sn-sync src="/api/events">
    <sn-event name="person_updated" resource="people" op="upsert" value="$event.person"></sn-event>
    <!-- after the removal: close the dialog if it shows that person (closing clears `sel`) -->
    <sn-event name="person_removed" resource="people" op="remove"
              then="sel?.id === $event.id && closeDialog('person')"></sn-event>
  </sn-sync>

  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="p in people">
      <li><button data-sn-on-click="sel = p; openDialog('person')" data-sn-text="p.name"></button></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
  <dialog id="person" data-sn-on-close="sel = null"><h2 data-sn-text="sel?.name"></h2></dialog>
</main>
```

### Optimistic toggle

```html
<sn-resource name="messages" src="/api/messages" key="id"></sn-resource>

<template data-sn-for="m in messages">
  <article>
    <span data-sn-text="m.subject"></span>
    <button data-sn-patch="/api/messages/{m.id}"
            data-sn-body="{is_flagged: !m.is_flagged}"
            data-sn-optimistic="merge(m, {is_flagged: !m.is_flagged})"
            data-sn-attr="{'aria-pressed': m.is_flagged ? 'true' : 'false'}">★</button>
  </article>
</template>
```

### Pagination in the URL: model, shared links and Back

```html
<!-- The page lives in the URL: ?page=3 is read at load and written back on every move. Page numbers are
     links (crawlable, a new tab, copy link); a click stays on the page and loads that page of the list. -->
<sn-resource name="articles" src="/api/articles" items="articles" total="count" key="slug"
  paginate="{ numbered: 'offset', size: 2, model: $url.page }"></sn-resource>

<ul>
  <template data-sn-for="a in articles"><li data-sn-text="a.title"></li></template>
</ul>
<nav aria-label="Pages">
  <button data-sn-on-click="page(articles, 'prev')" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !$meta.articles.hasPrev}">‹</button>
  <template data-sn-for="n in Array.from({ length: $meta.articles.pages ?? 0 }, (_, i) => i + 1)">
    <!-- the current link reads the page asked for ($url.page); the range below, the page shown ($meta) -->
    <a data-sn-text="n" data-sn-href="?page={n}" data-sn-attr="{ 'aria-current': n == (+$url.page || 1) ? 'page' : null }"></a>
  </template>
  <button data-sn-on-click="page(articles, 'next')" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !$meta.articles.hasNext}">›</button>
  <span data-sn-text="`${$meta.articles.from}–${$meta.articles.to} of ${$meta.articles.total}`"></span>
</nav>
```

### Typed resources, state and events

```html
<sn-resource name="contacts" src="/api/contacts" items="contacts" key="id" type="Contact[]"></sn-resource>

<sn-sync src="/api/events">
  <sn-event name="contact_updated" resource="contacts" op="upsert" value="$event.contact" type="ContactEvent"></sn-event>
</sn-sync>

<section data-sn-state="{ editing: /** @type {Contact|null} */ (null) }">
  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="c in contacts">
      <li>
        <span data-sn-text="c.name"></span>
        <small data-sn-text="c.email ?? 'no email'"></small>
        <button data-sn-on-click="editing = structuredClone(c)">Edit</button>
      </li>
    </template>
  </ul>
  <template data-sn-if="editing">
    <form data-sn-put="/api/contacts/{editing.id}" data-sn-body="editing"
          data-sn-then="upsert(contacts, $result); editing = null">
      <input data-sn-model="editing.name" required>
      <button>Save</button>
    </form>
  </template>
</section>
```

```ts
// src/sinter.types.ts
export interface Contact { id: number; name: string; email: string | null }
export interface ContactEvent { contact: Contact }
```

### Local actions: hash a file, then upload it

```html
<section data-sn-state="{ file: null, url: '', error: '' }">
  <sn-resource name="digest" call="sha256(file)" when="file"></sn-resource>

  <input type="file" data-sn-on-change="file = $el.files[0] ?? null; url = ''">
  <p data-sn-show="$meta.digest.loading">Hashing…</p>
  <code data-sn-text="digest"></code>

  <button data-sn-call="upload(file, digest)" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !digest}"
          data-sn-then="url = $result.url; error = ''" data-sn-catch="error = $error.message">Upload</button>
  <a data-sn-show="url" data-sn-attr="{href: url}">Uploaded</a>
  <p role="alert" data-sn-text="error"></p>
</section>
```

```js
// src/sinter.actions.js: functions pages call with data-sn-call and <sn-resource call>.
// The last argument is sinter's context; with JSDoc types, `sinter check` checks the calls.
/** @import { CallContext } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter' */

/**
 * The file's SHA-256 as hex; choosing another file aborts the running hash through ctx.signal.
 * @param {File} file
 * @param {CallContext} ctx
 * @returns {Promise<string>}
 */
export async function sha256(file, ctx) {
  const bytes = await file.arrayBuffer();
  ctx.signal.throwIfAborted();
  const hash = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', bytes);
  return [...new Uint8Array(hash)].map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
}

/**
 * ctx.request goes through the app's middleware (headers, 401 handling, allowed origins).
 * @param {File} file
 * @param {string} digest
 * @param {CallContext} ctx
 * @returns {Promise<{ url: string }>}
 */
export async function upload(file, digest, ctx) {
  const form = new FormData();
  form.append('file', file);
  form.append('sha256', digest);
  return /** @type {Promise<{ url: string }>} */ (ctx.request('/api/uploads', { method: 'POST', body: form }));
}
```

### More recipes

- Events that sometimes carry the item: apply it, or reload: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/partial-events.html
- Data a click loads: state and `when`, instead of a GET action: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/click-to-load.html
- Offline drafts: sent again once the connection is back: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/offline-draft.html
- Pagination: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/pagination.html
- Search in the URL: a model on $url, one history entry per search: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/url-search.html
- A multi-select filter in the URL: an array parameter: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/url-filter.html
- SignalR (or another transport) for <sn-sync>: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/signalr.html, https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/signalr-transport.js
- Cached list across page loads: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/cached-list.html
- Keyboard shortcuts: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/keyboard-shortcuts.html
- Row selection with Ctrl and Shift: logic in a helper, applied by the handler: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/row-select.html, https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/row-select.helpers.js
- Run an action from a handler: mark a mail read once its body has loaded, and a shortcut: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/run-action.html
- First paint: page chrome that renders before the script: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/first-paint.html
- Messages: m.key() from the inlang files, switching without a reload: https://github.com/tiaforge/sinter/blob/main/docs/recipes/messages.html

## Type checking

`npx sinter check` type-checks every expression with the project's TypeScript (pages and options come from the Vite config). `vite build` runs it too when the project has TypeScript (`typecheck: false` turns it off).

- `<sn-resource … type="Contact[]">`: the type of what `items` selects, using names exported by `src/sinter.types.ts`. `type="any"` opts out; no `type` is warning SN504.
- APIs: `sinter({ apis: { main: { base, openapi: 'openapi.yml', credentials, headers, defaults: { 'GET /articles': { items, total, key, type, query } }, operations: { … }, default: true } } })`. Pages write paths relative to an API: `src="/articles?tag={t}"`, `src="billing:/invoices"`, `data-sn-delete="/articles/{a.slug}"`, `src="site:/config.json"` (the page's own origin). Every path must be an operation the API declares (spec or `operations`) with the place's method (SN326), with declared and required query parameters, `paginate`'s included (SN327); an absolute URL is SN328. `items`/`total`/`key`/`type` come from `defaults`/`operations`: restating them is SN518 (same) or SN330 (different). `key` is never guessed: a list of objects without it is SN517. Each request carries its API's credentials and headers; `apiOf(url)` names the API in a middleware. `<sn-resource method="POST" body="{ q }">` loads with a POST (no cache, paginate, each). `npx sinter migrate --write` rewrites URLs into paths. Resources are typed from the operation's JSON response at `items`; every build checks `items`/`total` against the schema (SN308). Guide: docs/apis.md. The older `sinter({ openapi })` (deprecated) matches full `src` URLs and only warns (SN505).
- State takes a JSDoc cast where the literal is not enough: `data-sn-state="{ editing: /** @type {Contact|null} */ (null) }"`.
- Actions matched in the spec: `data-sn-body` is checked against the request schema, `$result` in `then` has the response type.
- `$result` in `<sn-resource then>` has the resource's type (`type`, OpenAPI, or a `call`'s result).
- `<sn-event … type="ContactEvent">` types the payload, the object the server sends: `value="$event.contact"` on a resource of `Contact[]` is `type="{ contact: Contact }"`; `value` must fit the resource's item (`op="upsert"`) or part of it (`op="merge"`), and `then` is checked against it. `$item` in `paginate`'s cursor has the resource's item type. No `type` on an event with payload expressions is warning SN506.
- In the URL, body, call arguments and confirm of an element `run('id')` starts (not a form), `$event` is `RunEvent<…>` (no event when run): guard reads with `$event && $event.shiftKey`.
- Strict mode (`sinter({ strict: true })`, or `SINTER_STRICT=1`): warnings fail `sinter check`, `vite build` (the type-checker's ones, SN504 and SN506, when it type-checks), pages in the dev server and `render()` in tests; runtime warnings are printed in the dev server's terminal and overlay. Run `sinter check --strict` after a change and fix what it reports rather than treating warnings as noise. `sinter({ strict: { allow: { SN504: 'reason' } } })` keeps a code a warning, with the reason. SN525–SN528 and SN533 (machine or network), SN507 and SN536 (heuristics) and runtime warnings that depend on the environment stay warnings. A test about a warning: `render(html, { strict: false })` and `warnings()`. docs/strict.md.
- SN509 (`run-cycle`) reports `then`/`catch` handlers that start each other again through `run()` (and `refresh()`), with every step.
- Errors are SN208 at the HTML position, with TypeScript's message. Null checks are off. In tests: `checkPage(html, { files, openapi })` from `@tiaforge-ui/sinter/check`; `render(html, { apis })` takes the APIs with parsed specs.

## First paint

The built page shows its chrome before the page module runs. The page bundle is `async` and may run while the body is still being parsed: app code at module top level must not read the body, and a custom element's `connectedCallback` must not read its children or later siblings. Guide: docs/first-paint.md.

- Build-time constants are written into the HTML: bindings outside templates that read only literal `data-sn-state` fields nothing writes, and `data-sn-for` over a constant list.
- An early script renders, before the first paint, the bindings outside `data-sn-for` templates that need no data (initial state, persisted values, `$locale`, helpers). Optional app code for it goes in `src/sinter.early.ts`; state it sets must be set again by the page bundle. Resources, `$url`, `$now`, `$meta`, loops and `relative()` wait for the page module (`date()`, `number()` and the other formatters are early; each early file has only those it calls), except a resource's loading state: `<template data-sn-if="$meta.people.loading && !people.length">` renders early. Keep heavy imports out of early code (`sinter({ firstPaint: { budget } })`, default 10000 bytes gzip).
- Keep page chrome outside data templates: `<template data-sn-if="user">` around the navigation hides it until the user has loaded.
- A page with nothing left to run (no state anything writes, no data, `$url`, helpers, handlers, actions, models or component scripts) ships no JavaScript. `sinter({ static: ['about.html', 'docs/**'] | true })` makes that a rule: a listed page that needs the runtime is SN322. Guide: docs/static-pages.md.
- Builds minify each page's HTML (`sinter({ minifyHtml: false })` turns it off; never in dev): comments, and white space the stylesheets show to render nothing, go before the page compiles. Do not put another HTML minifier or a CDN optimizer in front of sinter's pages: stripping its comments or white space breaks lists and branches. Guide: docs/minify.md.
- Page URLs: a page without `data-sn-path` is a directory's index (`about.html` is `/about/`; not `index.html`, `404.html`, `200.html`). Links in the markup to a page, by file or URL, are rewritten to its URL; links built at run time are not: write `'/task/?id=' + t.id`, not `'/task.html?id='`. A page with `data-sn-path` answers at exactly its absolute paths or patterns (`/article/:slug`, `/ /tag/:tag`, `/login`); its own directory URL is SN515. The build writes `_redirects` (`sinter({ redirects: false })`); `vite dev`, `vite preview` and sinter-axum follow the same rules.
- Canonical URLs: `sinter({ site: 'https://example.com' })`; `$site` is the origin with `base`, `$canonical` the page's URL (`<meta property="og:url" data-sn-attr="{ content: $canonical }">`); pages get `<link rel="canonical">`. Either name without `site` is SN323.
- Sitemap: with `site`, the build writes `sitemap.xml` with every page that may be indexed (not `noindex`, its canonical link its own URL), each language with its alternates. Pages whose path has parameters need their values: `sinter({ sitemap: { paths: { '/article/:slug': async () => slugs } } })` (a string per value, or `{ year, slug }`); without them they are left out. `sitemap: false` turns it off; a `public/sitemap.xml` is kept.
- Languages in the URL: `sinter({ localePrefix: true })` with the built-in messages (`baseLocale` among `locales`) builds each page once per language (`/en/about/`, `/de/about/`). `localeUrl('de')` is this page in German (`<a hreflang="de" data-sn-attr="{ href: localeUrl('de') }">`); assigning `$locale` there is SN203. `data-sn-path` is written without the prefix; `$url` excludes it.
- Reserved space: a `data-sn-for` outside templates over a paginated resource holds its `size` rows' space, sized from the stylesheets, until the data arrives; the build prints each paginated list without space and why. A list over late data in a box whose width follows its content keeps what follows hidden while its first rows load (3 s at most; `data-sn-wait="off"` on the box). SN529: give the box a width (`flex: 1 1 0`) or the rows one. SN530: an image without a height in such rows.
- Data requests start before the page module (preload or the early script) for resources whose `src` is same-origin or in `sinter({ origins: ['https://api.example.com'] })`; list API origins there, not in `configure({ origins })`. Early requests leave before request middleware runs, so when the config module may change requests (`configure({ request })`, `header()`) nothing is requested early, and a token middleware needs no `early="off"`. With an OpenAPI spec, `security` decides per operation: public or cookie ones are still preloaded. If you control the API, sign in with an `HttpOnly` session cookie rather than a token in localStorage: the browser sends it with early requests, so they keep working, and no script can read it.
- Next-page data: a link to another page of the app that the pointer rests on, focuses or presses loads that page's resources ahead (whose `src`/`when` read only `$url`, constants and helpers); give pages `data-sn-path` patterns so links match. `sinter({ prefetch: false })` turns it off; `<html data-sn-prefetch="off">` on a page that does something when it loads (logout). Chromium also gets Speculation Rules (`sinter({ prefetch: { html } })`), an inline script: a CSP sent as a header needs `'inline-speculation-rules'`. Page transitions: `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` and the same `data-sn-transition="'article-' + a.slug"` name on a list row and on the detail page (`'article-' + $url.slug`). Guide: docs/navigation.md.
- Same-page links: a plain click on a link to this page that changes only query parameters it reads stays on the page (a history entry; `$url` takes the link's query). Build the whole query: `href="?page=3"` drops the other parameters (SN519).
- Embedded data: `<script type="application/json" data-sn-resource="name">` in the head (filled by a server or middleware) renders in the first frame, rows included. `sinter({ embed: true })` with `import { embed } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/server'` does this for Hono, Bun, Deno and Workers: `export default { fetch: (await embed<Build>({ dir: 'dist', data: { … } })).wrap(app.fetch) }`. Guide: docs/server.md.
- Google Fonts links are downloaded and bundled at build time (`sinter({ fonts: false })` turns it off).
- Heavy packages: `sinter({ lazy: ['openpgp'] })` loads a package on first call. Import it as usual; every call of its exports must be waited for (`await`, `return`, `.then`, `void`); `new`, `instanceof`, constants, functions passed as values, side-effect imports and re-exports are SN324. A component script may use it freely (it loads with the component), and so may a helper module: it loads whole when a `data-sn-let` that calls one of its helpers is first read, the let is `undefined` until then, and calling its helpers anywhere but a let or a prop is SN324. `data-sn-import="openpgp"` loads it when an element renders, `data-sn-preload="openpgp"` adds modulepreload links. SN325: the package reached through another one, or a module both imported and lazily loaded. A chunk a deploy removed gives `$error.stale = true`. Guide: docs/lazy.md.
- `sinter({ firstPaint: false })` turns off the early script and reserved space; constants are still written in and pages with nothing to run still ship no JavaScript. Test with `firstPaint(html, { helpers, storage, early })` from the testing module (`early` stands for `src/sinter.early.ts`), and `render(html, { firstPaint: { early, afterEarly } })` for the takeover.

## Images

Write plain `<img src="./photo.jpg" alt="…">` (a local JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF, relative to the page or component): the build makes a `<picture>` with AVIF or WebP files for every screen, `width`/`height`, lazy loading after the first image and a placeholder color, sized from the stylesheets (write `sizes` yourself only where the CSS cannot be followed: `em`, `vh`, unequal grid tracks, `:hover`). Needs sharp; `sinter({ images: false })` turns it off. Guide: docs/images.md.

- `width`/`height` smaller than the source: a fixed box with 1x/2x files; a source with too few pixels for 2x is SN511. A fixed width from the stylesheets (Tailwind's `size-12` too) is a box as well.
- To crop: `width` and `height` of the box plus `style="object-fit: cover"` (and `object-position`). Another ratio without `object-fit` is SN512 (stretched).
- Images from the API: `sinter({ images: { remote: { url: 'https://img.example.com/{w}/{url}', origins: ['self'] } } })` (or a preset: `cloudflare`, `vercel`, `netlify`, `imgproxy:<base>`) gives `<img data-sn-attr="{src: c.avatar}">` a `srcset`. Tests: `render(html, { images: { remote }, css })`.
- CSS backgrounds (`background: url(./hero.jpg) center / cover`) get `image-set()`; use a source twice the largest width shown.
- Left as written: remote URLs, SVG, GIF, an `<img>` with `srcset`, inside your own `<picture>`, or with `data-sn-*` bindings.

## Messages

- With an inlang project (`project.inlang/settings.json`, message files `messages/{locale}.json` of plain `"key": "text with {param}"`), `m.key()` / `m.key({ param })` in markup are sinter's built-in messages. App code: `import { m } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/messages'`, typed by the generated `src/sinter.messages.d.ts`. Unknown keys are SN206, wrong or missing params SN208 (`sinter check`). Only `m.key`: `m[key]` or passing `m` on fails the build; a dynamic choice is a switch.
- The build emits one file per page and language with only the keys the page calls (markup and its modules); a missing translation is the base language, reported at build. No plurals or variants.
- Before the first paint the head script picks the language (localStorage `locale`, else `navigator.languages`, else the base), sets `<html lang>` and starts the page's language file without waiting for it; the base language's text is in the HTML, hidden for other languages until rendered (3 s at most): on every page that calls `m`, in its markup or in a helper, action or custom element it bundles. `$locale = 'de'` switches without a reload (stores the choice, loads that file, re-renders). Don't `configure({ locale })`: sinter is the locale source.
- Tests: `render(html, { messages: { en: {…}, de: {…} }, locale })`. An app without an inlang project ships none of this.

## Deploying streams

Each open EventSource holds one HTTP connection, and HTTP/1.1 allows 6 per origin: with more than 5 tabs open, pages stop loading. Serve streams over HTTP/2 (any TLS reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy) or use the WebSocket transport; dev builds warn about HTTP/1.1.

## Editors

`npx sinter lsp --stdio` is a language server for the project's HTML files: sinter's diagnostics as you type (components checked through the pages that use them), and with TypeScript 7 type errors, hover, completion in expressions, go to definition and a did-you-mean quick fix; "Extract to helper" moves an expression into a typed function of the helpers module. VS Code: the extension in `editors/vscode`. Setup for Neovim, Helix and Emacs: `docs/editors.md`. Every diagnostic links to its explanation in `docs/diagnostics.md`.

## Resources

`<sn-resource name src key>` is a named, page-wide cache of server data: the page reads it by name, it loads by itself (latest wins, shared requests, the typing pause), and `$meta.<name>` holds its status. `when` delays it, `cache` shows the last page load's data at once, `refresh="30s"` reloads it in the background, `for="a in accounts"` fans out one request per item, `call` feeds it from a function, `src="file:…"` or `content:` from the project at build time. Without `key` it is one object, `null` until loaded; a list the build knows is one (`type="string[]"`, the OpenAPI response at `items`, a `file:` list) is `[]` instead, so `tags.length` needs no `?.`. Guide: docs/resources.md.

## Actions

`data-sn-post`/`-put`/`-patch`/`-delete` or `data-sn-call` turn an element into a request: a form sends its fields, other elements `data-sn-body`; `data-sn-then`/`data-sn-catch` run after it, `data-sn-optimistic` shows the change at once, write-through applies the response by itself, and `run('id')` starts one from a handler. Dialogs, keyboard shortcuts, `data-sn-options` lists and row selection are here too. Guide: docs/actions.md.

## Pagination

`paginate="{ keyset: { before: $item.id }, size: 20 }"` loads a page at a time; `append` for load more, `numbered: true` (or `'offset'`) for page numbers, `model: $url.page` keeps the page in the URL. `page(messages, 'next')` moves; `$meta.<name>` has `hasPrev`, `hasNext`, `from`, `to`, `total`, `page`, `pages`. `params` and `directions` name the server's parameters, once per API. Guide: docs/pagination.md.

## Live updates

`<sn-sync src>` with `<sn-event name resource op value when then>` children turns server events (SSE, WebSocket, SignalR) into store changes: `upsert`, `merge`, `remove`, `refresh`. Reconnects go through the session probe, missed events are caught up by a reload, and `$meta.<name>.live` is the stream's state. Guide: docs/sync.md.

## Navigation

Between pages: the next page's data is requested while the pointer rests on a link (`prefetch: { data }`), Speculation Rules fetch or prerender its HTML (`prefetch: { html }`), and with `sinter({ swap: true })` a link swaps the next page in, keeping `data-sn-permanent` elements and streams; `data-sn-transition` names the page transitions. Same-page links and `navigate()` change only the URL's parameters a page reads. Guide: docs/navigation.md.

## APIs

`sinter({ apis: { main: { base, openapi, credentials, headers, defaults, operations, paginate } } })`: pages write paths relative to an API (`src="/contacts"`, `billing:/invoices`), checked against its spec; resources are typed from it and write-through knows its entities. `sinter migrate` moves an app's URLs to these paths. Guide: docs/apis.md.

## Pages without JavaScript

A page with nothing to run ships no JavaScript: its constant bindings are written into the HTML at build time. `sinter({ static: ['about.html'] })` makes that a build error to break (SN322); `<html data-sn-for="post in posts" data-sn-path="/blog/:slug">` builds one page per entry; `localePrefix` builds each page per language. Guide: docs/static-pages.md.

## Strict mode

`sinter({ strict: true })` (or `SINTER_STRICT=1`) fails `sinter check`, `vite build`, the dev server's pages and `render()` on warnings; `strict: { allow: { SN504: 'why' } }` keeps one code a warning. Warnings that depend on the machine or the network, and the heuristic ones, stay warnings. Guide: docs/strict.md.

## Configuration

The Vite plugin's options (`sinter({ … })`), the project's modules at fixed names (`src/sinter.helpers.ts`, `.actions`, `.config`, `.early`, `.types`, `.content`), `configure({ request, sessionProbe, onError, locale, transport, retry, confirm, fieldErrors })` in the config module. Helpers, formatters and state: docs/expressions.md; built-in messages: docs/messages.md. Guide: docs/configuration.md.

## Lazy packages

`sinter({ lazy: ['openpgp'] })` keeps a heavy package out of the page bundle: it loads when an element with `data-sn-import` is rendered, or on the first call; `data-sn-preload` starts it earlier. The build measures what moved. Guide: docs/lazy.md.

## Component libraries

`sinter({ libraries: ['@acme/ui'] })` names packages whose `package.json` has `"sinter": "./sinter"`: their public components are tags in the app, under the library's prefix; their helpers come in through a namespace. A library checks itself through fixture pages in `fixtures/`, with its modules beside them. Guide: docs/libraries.md.

## Security

Expressions reach only a closed set of names, so markup cannot run arbitrary code; URLs are checked against `origins`, bindings to `href` and `src` refuse `javascript:`, and scripts, the early files and fonts are files a CSP can allow. Trusted Types and CSP nonces are supported. Guide: docs/security.md.

## The server layer

`@tiaforge-ui/sinter/server`'s `embed()` (and sinter-axum, Sinter.AspNetCore) fill each page's embedded-data placeholders per request, so the first frame has the data: it reads the build's `sinter-embed.json`, fetches each placeholder's request (from the API, or `data: { name: fn }`), and streams the page. Guide: docs/server.md.

## Components with a script

A component with `<name>.ts` beside its HTML has a script: a class over the base the build declares, with `this.props`, `this.refs`, `this.emit()` and the page's store (`this.app`), for what markup cannot do (a canvas, a third-party widget). Guide: docs/islands.md.

## Minified HTML

Builds minify each page's HTML (`minifyHtml: false` turns it off): comments go, and white space the CSS shows to render nothing; `render(html, { minifyHtml: true, css })` tests it. Guide: docs/minify.md.

## Testing

To try a page and test what it does, start here, before a browser script: `npx sinter render incident.html --url /incidents/3 --api http://localhost:3000 --storage token=abc --select "#status=open" --click "#save"` runs the page against your running API (or mocks: `--api mocks.json` with `mockRequests` routes; both may be given, mocks first), with the project's modules (config middleware, helpers, components), and prints each request with its headers and status, the rendered markup, each resource's `loading`/`error`/value, history pushes and replaces, the storage keys the page read (a `--storage` key nothing read is a warning naming the keys it did read), and the warnings, then what each step changed (`--click`, `--input sel=text`, `--select`, `--check`, `--submit`, `--back`, `--wait 5s`, `--emit event=json`; `--show sel`, `--json`). Exit code 1 when a request failed or the page warned. It runs on jsdom (in the starter; elsewhere `npm i -D jsdom`): layout, CSS and browser quirks still need a browser. Guide: docs/testing.md#sinter-render.

Then write a test next to the markup, to keep it working. `@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing` compiles the page with the real compiler and mounts it:

- `render(html, { requests, streams, url, locale, now, helpers, actions, files, components, layouts, scripts, storage, session, firstPaint })` → `{ root, app, state, flush, settle, advance, navigations, window }`. The page is compiled as a build compiles it (build-time constants, decided branches, unrolled loops). `state(el).update(fn)` writes the scope around `el` and re-renders it; it throws for a field nothing on the page writes, which the build made a constant (write it from a handler instead). Pass one `memoryStorage()` as `session` to two renders to test what carries over between page loads (the `cache` attribute). A full document keeps its `<html>` attributes, so state and `data-sn-persist` on `<html>` work as in the browser.
- `mockRequests({ 'GET /api/x': json | {status, body} | (call) => … })`: records `calls`; responses are held until `settle()`; an unmatched request fails the test and lists the routes.
- `mockStream()`: `emit(name, payload)`, `drop()`, `connected`. A stream URL with no mock uses the transport from `configure({ transport })`, so a custom transport can be tested over a fake connection (see the SignalR recipe).
- `flush()` runs the scheduler (optimistic changes are visible), `settle()` finishes requests, queues and debounces, `advance(ms)` moves sinter's clock.
- `firstPaint(html, { helpers, files, storage, early })` → `{ root, html }`: the page as the browser shows it before the page module runs (build-time constants, then the early chunk). `render(…, { firstPaint: { early, afterEarly } })` mounts over that first paint; `afterEarly` runs in between, so a test can watch what mounting changes.
